html:
In February 1221 a Mongol army under Tolui, son of Genghis Khan, took Merv, in Turkmenistan, and destroyed it, killing almost all of its people.

It was part of the Mongol war against the Khwarazmian Empire, after the invasion of 1219. The city surrendered after a short siege on a promise of mercy. Instead the people were led out and killed, save some craftsmen taken away. Writers of the time gave numbers in the hundreds of thousands or more, surely too high but a sign of the horror.

The canals and dams of the oasis were wrecked, and the region took centuries to recover. Merv shrank to a small town. The destruction of Merv, Nishapur and Urgench was among the worst of the Mongol conquests.
sum: In February 1221 a Mongol army under Tolui, son of Genghis Khan, took Merv, in Turkmenistan, and destroyed it, killing almost all of its people.
